preamble: Debuccalization of the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] to a glottal fricative. In the Slavic g-spirantization area, *g became [ɣ] and then a glottal fricative; Upper Sorbian (14th century) ends in voiceless /h/ (hora 'mountain' < *gora), while Czech, Slovak, Ukrainian and Belarusian have voiced [ɦ].

examples.to: hora, with /h/ a voiceless glottal fricative
examples.note: The spirantization of Slavic /g/ to /h/ is an areal feature reaching Upper Sorbian in the 14th century; Lower Sorbian keeps góra. Upper Sorbian /h/ is listed as voiceless [h].

sources: Wikipedia (2025). History of the Czech language. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Czech_language
